Run Parallelized BLAST

Source: R/parallel_blast.R
parallel_blast.Rd

Search a set of sequences against one or more BLAST databases, using the cores and RAM given. The search strategy is chosen automatically (see blast_strategy()): the sequences are grouped in batches, and each blastn process searches a whole batch, so the database is read once per batch instead of once per sequence.

The progress bar shows the estimated time left (ETA), computed from the batches already finished. With background = TRUE the search runs in a separate process and the function returns at once; see blast_job().

Usage

parallel_blast(
  query_seqs,
  db_path,
  ...,
  total_cores = 1L,
  ram_gb = NULL,
  num_alignments = 10L,
  search_alignments = 50L,
  perc_id = 80L,
  perc_qcov_hsp = 80L,
  search_qcov_hsp = 50L,
  check_n = 10L,
  check_tolerance = 0.5,
  rank_by = c("similarity", "identity", "bitscore"),
  uninformative = uninformative_references(),
  output = c("long", "wide"),
  num_threads = NULL,
  batch_size = NULL,
  mt_mode = NULL,
  task = NULL,
  background = FALSE,
  job_dir = NULL,
  log_dir = NULL,
  retry_times = 3L,
  blast_type = "blastn",
  verbose = c("progress", "silent", "cmd", "output", "full"),
  env_name = "blastr-blast-env",
  out_file = deprecated(),
  out_RDS = deprecated()
)

Arguments

query_seqs

Character vector with sequences.

db_path

Path(s) to the formatted BLAST database(s). Several databases (a vector, or one string separated by spaces) are searched together, the smallest first.

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

total_cores

Number of CPU cores (threads) to use in total.

ram_gb

RAM available for the search, in GB. Used to decide whether the database fits in memory. NULL uses the total RAM of the machine.

num_alignments

Number of hits to keep for each sequence. Defaults to 10.

search_alignments

Number of subjects BLAST keeps during the search (-max_target_seqs). BLAST cuts its list of subjects before the perc_qcov_hsp filter, so asking only for num_alignments can lose valid hits. BLASTr searches max(num_alignments, search_alignments) subjects and keeps the num_alignments best ones that pass the filters. In the benchmark, 50 instead of 10 added about 5% to the time.

perc_id

Lowest identity percentage cutoff.

perc_qcov_hsp

Query coverage per HSP (percent) expected of a good hit. Hits below it are kept and flagged (low_qcov), not removed: removing them inside BLAST hides a closer reference that covers a bit less of the query (common with partial reference sequences) and promotes a worse one. The coverage still weighs in the rank through the Similarity score. Defaults to 80.

search_qcov_hsp

Lowest query coverage per HSP (percent) used by BLAST (-qcov_hsp_perc); hits below it are not returned. Defaults to 50. Set it to perc_qcov_hsp to remove the hits below perc_qcov_hsp, as in earlier versions.

check_n

Number of best hits compared by Check ID (see check_hits()). Defaults to 10.

check_tolerance

Difference from the best hit, in the units of rank_by, under which hits are tied ("at best"). Defaults to 0.5.

rank_by

Criterion to rank the hits of each sequence: "similarity" (default, the Similarity score, see similarity_score()), "identity" or "bitscore". Ties are broken by identity, coverage, bitscore and BLAST order. BLAST orders its hits by e-value/bitscore, which favours longer alignments, so its first hit is not always the most similar one. In a calibration on plant barcodes of known genus (ITS2, rbcL) and on 1257 GenBank references of six markers searched without themselves, ranking by Similarity score or identity picked the right taxon significantly more often than bitscore (genus: 72% and 76% against 62%), with no significant difference between them.

uninformative

Table of the references that do not inform the identification (uncultured, environmental, metagenomes, vectors, ...; see uninformative_references()): the table shipped with BLASTr (default), a path to another one, a data frame, or NULL to treat all hits alike (informative NA, not evaluated). The hits are flagged (informative, uninformative_category) and ranked among the informative ones, so rank, at_best, Check ID and blast_lca() use only those; a sequence whose hits are all uninformative keeps its best ones, ranked among themselves. Uninformative hits take subjects of the search, so a sequence of a poorly known group needs a larger search_alignments.

output

"long" (default): one row per hit. "wide": one row per sequence, with the summary of blast_summary() and the first num_alignments hits side by side (1_ is the best one).

num_threads, batch_size, mt_mode

Override the automatic strategy: threads per blastn process, sequences per batch and BLAST+ multithreading mode (0, 1 or 2). NULL (default) chooses automatically.

task

BLAST task (-task), e.g. "megablast" (the blastn default), "dc-megablast" or "blastn". NULL uses the BLAST default.

background

If TRUE, start the search in the background and return a job (see blast_job()) instead of the results.

job_dir

Directory for the job files. Defaults to a temporary directory (removed at the end) in the foreground, and to a new directory in the BLASTr cache in the background.

log_dir

Directory where a BLASTr_logs folder keeps a log of the searches (number and lengths of the sequences, database size, strategy, time, CPU time and percentage of identifications). NULL uses the option BLASTr.log_dir or the environment variable BLASTR_LOG_DIR; with none set, nothing is logged. See blast_log_path().

retry_times

Number of times to retry failed BLAST jobs. Defaults to 3 attempts.

blast_type

BLAST+ executable to be used on search.

verbose

"progress" (default) shows the progress and ETA; "silent" shows nothing. "cmd", "output" and "full" also show the chosen strategy.

env_name

The name of the conda environment used to run command-line tools. Defaults to "blastr-blast-env".

out_file

Deprecated. Path to output .csv file on an existing directory.

out_RDS

Deprecated. Path to output RDS file on an existing directory.

Value

With output = "long", a tibble with one row per hit, best first: Sequence, rank (1 = best; tied hits share the rank), tie (the rank is shared), at_best (within check_tolerance of the best hit), low_qcov (qcovhsp below perc_qcov_hsp), informative and uninformative_category (see uninformative), blast_rank (order given by BLAST), subject, subject header, staxid, identity, Similarity score, qcovhsp, nident, length, mismatches, gaps, query start, query end, subject start, subject end, subject strand, e-value and bitscore. The first num_alignments hits are kept (informative ones, when there are), plus all the hits at best and the uninformative hits among the first num_alignments of all (after the ranked ones, with rank NA). A sequence without hits has one row with NA hit fields. The summary per sequence (Check ID, ...) comes from blast_summary().

With output = "wide", one row per sequence: Sequence, the summary of blast_summary() and, for each hit k from 1 to num_alignments in rank order, the hit fields prefixed by k_.

The attribute BLASTr_metadata keeps the parameters, the strategy, the BLAST command (blast_cmd, without the sequences), the BLAST version, the date of each database and the exit codes (see exit_codes()). With background = TRUE, a blastr_job.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
dna_fasta_path <- fs::path_package(
  "BLASTr", "extdata", "minimal_db_blast",
  ext = "fasta"
)
temp_db_path <- fs::path_temp("minimal_db_blast")
make_blast_db(fasta_path = dna_fasta_path, db_path = temp_db_path)
query_seqs_string <- c(
  "CTAGCCATAAACTTAAATGAAGCTATACTAA",
  "ACTCGTTCGCCAGAGTACTACAAGCGAAAG"
)
blast_res <- parallel_blast(
  query_seqs = query_seqs_string,
  db_path = temp_db_path
)
blast_res

# in the background
job <- parallel_blast(query_seqs_string, temp_db_path, background = TRUE)
blast_job_status(job)
blast_res <- blast_job_result(job)
} # }
